# april decks

## crystal tarot and the basic RWS
i picked the crystal tarot for its vibrant green, it feels springy. the RWS was simply one of the leftover decks that didn't get its own definite month, so i paired it up with the crystal as a "safe" bet, seeing as the crystal tarot uses the picard system which i'm not all that comfortable with.
well, my "safe bet" deck immediately went back on the shelf. while i can read it easily, the art is just extremely off-putting, i just never feel like reaching for it. the crystal tarot is much more attractive and appealing to look at, but doesn't speak too clearly. and to be fair, i have no real interest in learning the picard system. i'm trying to read "despite" it, not integrating it.
initially i tried to deal with the elemental mismatch (air for cups and water for swords) by reading it like i'd do any pip deck. except i realized that i do still heavily lean on elemental associations there. which makes me want to make the effort - when i do reach some marseille decks in this challenge - to finally read them a bit more... hmm... literally? less-esoterically. as they were probably read early on. but i did work out my own way of navigatin

# march decks

## ritual tarot and the thoth
i picked both of these for their "Pow!" aries sort of feeling, to welcome in the spring and the new astrological year. but it quickly turned out i see them more as magical tools than just plain old tarot decks. the effect was twofold:
1. i followed a rabbit hole of thoth creators that pointed me back towards mysticism, which resulted in a renewed, inspired spiritual practice
2. when i wanted to just fool around with some cards, i reached instead for regular old playing cards, so that was quite fun.
in effect, the month itself wasn't all that much about tarot. as for my deck impressions - both of these are "good" decks. i used the ritual tarot a bit for introspective readings and what Esther from mindful tarot calls "wobble readings". i love the imagery, there's something primal and universal about it. using images of ancient art and artifacts together with landscape photography makes the art feel like it taps into a broad current of humanity. there's a sense of belonging and togetherness, both with other people and with the earth itself. at the same time the predominant colors seem to be blue and black, which to me grants it a bit of

=> /u/clseibold/28718 🚀 clseibold [🛂] · 2025-05-12 at 17:39:
While I agree that the web stuff is getting ridiculous, it's factually incorrect to say "CSS was invented to fix HTML", and JS was invented to fix HTML/CSS. CSS wasn't invented to "fix" HTML, it was invented to style HTML separately so that you could apply different styles to the same page. And JS was invented to make pages more dynamic. Has nothing to do with "fixing" HTML or CSS.

It seems the article is being very anachronistic in saying this; they see problems with HTML, therefore CSS *must have* been invented to "fix" HTML. In reality, the problems that the article's writer might see with HTML are not the same problems that people saw during the time CSS was invented.

I tend to be along the anti-web-technologies side for most things; I don't want HTML and CSS crap in all my applications.

##	●● Patents on Life Are a Cancer

Posted in Patents at 3:00 pm by Dr. Roy Schestowitz

Summary: The subject of patents on life is being brought up again by several blogs of patent maximalists; they seem to forget or simply ignore the whole purpose of patents

THE only class of patents we strongly object to other than software patents is life patents (or patents on life). It’s no coincidence that Section 101 in the United States is based on several Supreme Court cases which deal with patents on life and patents on business methods/software (Myriad, Mayo, Alice). Some things do not deserve patents (neither at the EPO nor at the USPTO) because societal benefit of these cannot be proven. Patenting just for the sake of having more patents is misguided; limits need to be imposed/enforced somewhere. Patents actually derive value from scarcity, not from overabundance.
